pure-announcement.rationale: It is a marketing teaser for Atlassian's own survey report, not a product launch or release note, and it does carry a transferable claim about coordination costs.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts (MCP platforms, evals, wikis, skills, context layer) cover team-level coordination costs of individual AI adoption.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The claims trace to a named survey (12,035 knowledge workers, 173 executives, Jan-Feb 2026) whose report a reader can consult, even if it is vendor self-reported data.

durability.rationale: The one durable kernel — individual AI speedups shift the bottleneck to team coordination — is buried under 2026-vintage survey percentages ($161B, 89%, 5.6x) that will be superseded by next year's edition.

actionability.rationale: It tells a reader that coordination matters but gives no mechanism or practice to adopt — the concrete 'new ways of working' are withheld behind the full report.

atomicity.rationale: Despite duplicated sections, the note carries exactly one idea — the fragmentation tax on team coordination — statable in a single paragraph without Atlassian's framing.
